en: "Can you keep quiet? Can you keep a secret?"
note: Choice prompt (44 chars); repeats the question of 6249. Check prompt width in game.
Yes branch of 6251.

en: "...You're honest to the point of stupid.{w}At the very least, you're not cut out to be merchants.{w}But I like that. Come on, humor me for a bit."{w}
note: No branch of 6251: the party honestly admits they can't keep a secret. [JP] kept with its edge ('honest to the point of stupid').

en:
"I've got some items that carry
the Caron brand name right in their names."{w}

"They should all perform pretty well, but between
the lack of advertising and them looking way too cute,
you adventurers won't give them a second look."{w}{p}"I guess sweaty types like you
would rather have some rugged design, huh?"{w}

"But a safe, run-of-the-mill design like you see everywhere
won't pass as my brand.{w}So I stopped making them for you lot."{w}{p}"I figured I'd make them cuter and cuter
and sell them as fashion items
to the younger generation."{w}{p}"And the place I set my sights on was Rubenburg.{w}That place is crawling with little brats, right?"{w}
note: [JP] = 'little brats'. [JP] = 'you lot' as in slice_029.

en:
"If I can just get the school store to stock them,
they're guaranteed to sell like crazy!"{w}
note: [JP] = 'the school store' (Rubenburg's).
[JP] inside a quote -> single quotes.
[JP]...[JP] = reported speech; 'They said' restored.

en: "Seriously, you've got to be kidding me!{w}They want a mere merchant to go fight?"{w}

"At first I thought it was just an excuse to turn down the contract,
but that vice principal said it with a straight face.{w}That makes it even worse!"{w}
note: [JP] = Kathleen (named in 6279); no pronoun used.

en:
"So here's the favor I wanted to ask:
I want you to go fight in my place.{w}Dressed head to toe in the Caron brand, of course."{w}
"Next time you come, don't bring any items at all.{w}Got it? You absolutely have to win, okay!?"{w}
"Looking good, looking good~{w}Even I'm smitten with how it turned out!"{w}
note: ♪ -> '~'. [JP] = 'Even I'm smitten with how it turned out'.

en: "Now hurry up and go win!{w}Your target is the vice principal, Kathleen!"{w}
note: [JP] = 'the vice principal, Kathleen' (glossary: Vice Principal Kathleen).

en:
"Left your stuff behind? Looks like you're ready."{w}{p}"Okay then,
I'm handing over the Caron brand items.{w}Well, they're only prototypes, though."{w}
"There, all equipped!"{w}
{0E}      *    You've been cursed!    *      {0F}{w}
note: Centred system banner; padding approximates the source (check centring in game).

en: "What did you expect? They're prototypes.{w}Quit your grumbling and go win like that!{w}Your target is the vice principal, Kathleen!"{w}
note: Source typo [JP] read as [JP].

en: "Hey, come on.{w}I told you to come empty-handed, didn't I?{w}Go on, hurry up and get ready!"{w}
"Welcome back! Looks like you pulled it off!"{w}

"Vice Principal Kathleen came by just now
and agreed to sign the contract!!{w}Yaaaaay!!"{w}
note: Built to avoid a pronoun for Kathleen (gender unknown).

en: "And the finished version just got done, too.{w}Now my brand name will thunder across the land!!{w}Thank you!!"{w}
note: [JP] = 'the finished version' (vs the prototypes).

en:
"Ugh, I'm beat..."{w}{p}"See, the Caron brand's a big hit.{w}Being a hit is great and all, but everyone
keeps nagging me to do this, do that."{w}

"Well, I'm happy about it, though!{w}Maybe I'll go tease that smelly shop
to blow off some steam."{w}
note: [JP] = 'that smelly shop'; which shop is meant is not stated (possibly a rival shop seen elsewhere). Kept literal.

en: "Would you like to hear one too?"
note: [JP] = 'Would you (all) like to hear one too?'

en: "Then, if you'll excuse me... Ahem."{w}

"We have confirmed the names
of six gods."{w}{p}"The god who creates life -- Orses, god of life-creation.{w}The god of change and pleasure -- Sarijana, god of change.{w}The god of death and endings -- Rogera, god of Dark Oblivion."{w}{p}"These are the gods who govern life.
Next..."{w}{p}"The god who creates space -- Semnadoc, god of subspace.{w}The god who governs time -- Sinhanicol, god of time.{w}The god who governs existence -- Dehain, god of existence."{w}{p}"These are the gods who govern
the order of things."{w}{p}"Theologians surmise that among these six
there is one chief god."{w}{p}"However, no decisive record remains
of who that chief god actually is."{w}{p}"Conjecture goes no further than
that it is either Orses or Dehain."{w}{p}"Even so, it is thought that among the gods,
the one with the greatest authority
is most likely Dehain."{w}{p}"This is because everything in this world
is said to be unable to exist
without Dehain's approval."{w}
note: Titles from the glossary: god of life-creation, god of change, god of Dark Oblivion, [JP] = god of subspace, god of time, god of existence. 'The god who X -- Name, title' keeps both the gloss and the title the source gives. [JP] = 'the order of things'.

en: "Would you like to hear more?"

"Orses is the god of truly equal love.
As the god who brings forth life, Orses must pour
unsparing love upon every created being."{w}{p}"Sarijana, it seems, helped Orses in the work
of creating life -- up to a point."{w}{p}"I say 'up to a point' because at some point,
Sarijana seems to have begun acting against
the will of the world of the gods."{w}{p}"What came of it
has not been handed down to our age."{w}{p}"There is a research report suggesting
that Orses and Dehain
were in dispute over something."{w}{p}"Whether Sarijana's turning against the gods
stemmed from the conflict between those two gods,
we do not yet know."{w}{p}"And then there is Semnadoc, whom this Cathedral reveres."{w}{p}"Semnadoc is the god who governs space,
and has left us many teachings to save our hearts,
such as 'Let there be smiles upon the land.'"{w}{p}"I myself was moved by those teachings,
and so, in this way, I have the honor of spreading
Semnadoc's teachings to all of you."{w}
note: Names repeated instead of pronouns (gods' genders unknown). [JP] = 'turning against the gods'. [JP] = 'Let there be smiles upon the land.' [JP] = 'Semnadoc' (lead convention).

en: "Would you care to hear more?"
note: [JP] variant of 6317; slightly different wording to keep the rows distinct.

en:
"Now, as for those who belong to the demon world.{w}They are beings at the opposite pole from the gods, but..."{w}{p}"In truth, there are no records at all
of where they come from
or what they intend to do."{w}{p}"Among what we call monsters are those born
in this land just as we were, those that came
from the demon world, and then..."{w}{p}"It is rumored that some of them
may even be messengers
of the gods."{w}{p}"It seems our imagination
can reach only so far."{w}{p}"But that we live embraced
by the love of the gods
is surely an unshakable truth."{w}{p}"Well,
it seems that is all I can tell you."{w}{p}"Now that you understand the gods more deeply,
may good fortune be with you."{w}
note: [JP] = 'the demon world' (not in glossary).

en:
"I understand.
Let us save the talk for another time."{w}
"Thank you for listening so attentively."{w}

"I am Mersenne, and I serve
as bishop of this Cathedral."{w}
note: Source says [JP] (bishop) here, though the glossary and 6342 make him an archbishop ([JP]). Kept 'bishop' as written; lead may prefer 'archbishop' for consistency.

en:
"Many people visit this town,
whether as pilgrims or as sightseers.{w}The town prospers thanks to everyone's offerings."{w}

"By rights,
we should not be taking money at all..."{w}

"Faith and running a business --
that must be the eternal dilemma of the clergy."{w}{p}"So, as what small service I can offer,
I make a point of speaking directly
with everyone who visits the Cathedral."{w}

note: First question is put to the party. [JP] = 'oracle' as in slice_029. [JP] = 'archbishop in history'.

en:
"Of course, such miracles
should not happen all that often, but...{w}It's a lonely state of affairs, all the same."{w}
"Hm?{w}Then what are my oracles really, you ask?{w}Intuition. Spiritual intuition. Haha!"{w}
note: [JP] = 'Intuition. Spiritual intuition.' ([JP] completes the noun).

en:
"Say 'spiritual' and it sounds
the part, doesn't it?{w}Well, keep that under wraps. Under wraps."{w}
note: [JP] repeated as 'Under wraps.' twice.

en: "No matter how hard things get, never forget to smile.{w}That is Semnadoc's teaching."{w}

"Do you know of the Edumo?{w}Being adventurers, I'm sure you do."{w}{p}"I was attacked by them once myself,
while I was out spreading the faith."{w}{p}"I tried to fight them
with the help of Semnadoc's power, but..."{w}{p}"When I spoke Semnadoc's name,
one of the Edumo, an especially large one,
laughed at me with scorn."{w}{p}"'...Semnadoc is retired now,'
it said."{w}{p}"It seems the seats of the gods have changed
in many ways over time, and the six gods we know
are different from those of today."{w}{p}"Incidentally, I hear
the current god of space is one called Void."{w}
note: The large Edumo is a monster: 'it'. [JP] = 'is retired now'.

en:
"Our own Semnadoc has apparently already
stepped down as god of space...{w}It is hard to believe."{w}
note: [JP] = 'Our own Semnadoc' (no honorific per lead).

en:
"But faith is a funny thing.{w}Being told that our god has already retired
makes me long for our god all the more."{w}{p}"I wonder, are my prayers being heard?"{w}
note: [JP] repeated as 'our god' to avoid a pronoun for Semnadoc.

en: "Forgive me for talking about such things.{w}But I felt that I could tell all of you."{w}
You offered a prayer to Semnadoc, god of space.{w}
note: [JP] = 'god of space' (glossary).

en: "An oracle, is it? Very well.{w}Then let us begin."{w}
"Haaaaaaahhh--!!"{w}
"May fortune be with you!!"{w}
note: [JP]: Mersenne uses [JP] here, singular 'you' is fine in English.

en: Hisbert

note: {0E}/{0F} kept around the second ellipsis as in the source. [JP] = 'cute little lambs' (glossary personality note).

en: "You came back again?"{w}
"Sigh...{w}Honestly, you hopeless children."{w}
note: [JP] = 'you hopeless children' (fond exasperation).

en: "Hm?{w}What do I mean by 'again'?{w}Never mind, never mind. Don't worry about it."{w}{p}"This is Elminage.{w}And I am Hisbert. Nice to meet you."{w}

"Elminage is the place that records every event
that has ever happened in the worlds
brought forth by the gods."{w}{p}"This may sound outlandish to you, but
besides Finas Rade, there exist
a great many other spaces and lands."{w}{p}"My role is to organize
the information of Elminage."{w}{p}"The information that drifts in is vast...
Even as I look at you here before me
and listen to your words,"{w}{p}"one of my eyes and one of my ears
are constantly taking in infinite facts.{w}Even now, right here in this very place."{w}{p}"From every war that has broken out in those spaces
to the first person you ever fell in love with..."{w}{p}"Everything is recorded
in Elminage, and converges here."{w}{p}"Ufufu, surprised?{w}But don't worry.
I'm merely an onlooker."{w}{p}"The System is not permitted to interfere
with the physical world.{w}That is the law of Elminage."{w}{p}"No matter what calamity or tragedy occurs,
all I can do is watch."{w}{p}"In exchange,
even if the gods abandon you,
I will never take my eyes off you."{w}{p}"I'm always watching over you, you know."{w}{p}"Now, shall we continue our talk?
There's a lot you want to ask, isn't there?"{w}
note: Sentence split across pages 4-5 kept split (comma, then lower case). [JP] = 'the System' (Elm3: Elminage System). [JP] = 'the physical world'. [JP] read as plural 'the gods'.

en:
"A great being.{w}But not one I'd call your ally."{w}{p}"You are allowed to exist
because of 'a certain one's remorse.'"{w}{p}"I can't tell you any more than that. I'm sorry."{w}
note: Answer to a talk topic not in the script (keyword menu); the subject of [JP] cannot be verified, so no name or pronoun is added. [JP] = 'a certain one's remorse'.

en:
"The Kin of Darkness...{w}What makes someone Kin of Darkness is hard to say, but..."{w}{p}"They are those born of darkness
and bound by fate to destruction."{w}{p}"When a new world is born
by the hands of the gods,
they come in full force to conquer it."{w}{p}"Besides the Contrachio affair,
you must have seen plenty of other crises, right?"{w}{p}"Be on your guard.{w}Let it slip, and Void's hounds
will devour your land whole."{w}{p}"...Though I believe that you
will surely overcome them."{w}
note: [JP] kept ambiguous ('bound by fate to destruction': destined to destroy or to be destroyed). [JP] = 'Void' (no honorific). [JP] object read as the crises/threat ('them').

en:
"A land young, yet old.{w}Over a mind-boggling span of time,
your land has come to exist."{w}
note: Source has no closing punctuation before the first {w}; a period added.

en: "Supported by much love and sincerity, mind you.{w}That's all I can tell you for now."{w}

"Keep searching. For the traces of creation.{w}I believe that you can surely fulfill
the promise made so very long ago."{w}
note: [JP] = 'the traces of creation'.

en:
"......{w}Oh, right, I have to sort the books."{w}{p}"Sorry,
it looks like I don't have time to deal with you.{w}Some other time."{w}
note: [JP] = 'sort the books' (also 6395).

en: Will you watch Hisbert sort the books?
note: Choice prompt, 38 chars; shorten to 'Watch Hisbert sort the books?' (29) if it does not fit.

en: You stepped away from Hisbert so as not to disturb her.{w}
note: 'her' = Hisbert (female in glossary).

en:
As if ignoring you,
Hisbert began picking up books.{w}

"Ugh. It's all jumbled up.{w}I need to put these in proper order."{w}{p}"Let's see... control number... this one's unregistered.{w}Zefkaka: Urna. System: Rade 301."{w}{p}"A land made by Orses, god of life-creation,
where life arose, but which Dehain
did not approve. How nostalgic."{w}{p}"And this one is control number 304972.{w}Zefkaka: Fiona. System: Noris 487."{w}{p}"A land made by Dehain, god of existence.{w}It was approved, but
life never arose there."{w}{p}"Well, of course -- it was made unilaterally
after a falling-out with the god of life-creation."{w}{p}"Oh, the system changes partway through.{w}System: Rade 301.{w}There's a note saying it was rewritten."{w}{p}"Why would it have been tampered with?"{w}{p}"Hmmm..."{w}
note: Registry format: [JP] = 'System: Rade 301' (and 'Noris 487'), matching the decimal in 6405 (304972.301 / .487). [JP] = 'control number', [JP] = 'Zefkaka' (glossary). [JP] rendered 'made unilaterally' to avoid a pronoun for Dehain. Gods without honorific.
One sentence split across pages 2-3: cut at the same point. [JP] = 'New Land' (glossary). [JP] = 'Orses and Sarijana' ([JP] read as 'and').
[JP] is sarcastic: 'so considerate as to'.

en:
"Fiona Noris,
control number 304972.487..."{w}{p}"was fused with Urna Rade, the unapproved land,
and changed to Fiur Rade,
control number 304972.301..."{w}{p}"So it was only natural that Orses, god of life-creation,
and Sarijana, god of change, who caused all this trouble,
were sent to the Horizon."{w}{p}"But Sarijana, never one to go quietly,
scattered something called the Deplus factor
on the way out, as I recall."{w}{p}"There were even claims that I'd let the spread
of this factor slide on purpose, and the first
no-confidence motion since Sabra's was raised."{w}
note: Sentence split across pages 1-2 kept split. [JP] = 'only natural that ... were sent'. [JP] = 'as I recall' (no pronoun for Sarijana). [JP] read as 'the first no-confidence motion since Sabra's' (Sabra = earlier librarian per glossary).

en: "Honestly, what an infuriating business!!"{w}

"This land's record is quite thick.{w}For a land so unstable, latently holding
a second Zefkaka, it sure lasted a long time."{w}{p}"...But in the end, it came to an end after all.{w}End time: 61043891."{w}{p}"Oh, how unusual.{w}There's a land with the exact same start time.{w}That land is control number 712612, system..."{w}
note: [JP] = 'a second Zefkaka' (glossary capital kept; glossary note allows lowercase for a common noun - lead's call). Deliberate trail-off kept.
[JP] = 'chief god' (as in 6316). [JP] = 'creating the Eld'.

en:
"A special land was planned for creating the Eld,
and lands with little chance of producing the Eld
were weeded out, one after another."{w}{p}"Among them was a land called Belnaf,
of the Arana system.{w}A rare land, devout and peaceful..."{w}
note: [JP] read as singular ('A special land'); number not settled by the source. [JP] = 'Arana' (glossary: Belnaf Arana). [JP] = 'weeded out'.
